title: ConsumerContext & StepUpProof — shared definitions used by vault tasks that hit the policy engine
description: Reused by vault/proxy-login, vault/release, and any future vault task that needs to feed situational context to the maintainer's policy engine or carry the response to a step-up demand. Producer-supplied fields are advisory — the maintainer cross-checks anything security-relevant against its own state.

deviceId.description: Device-binding id assigned at registration. The maintainer cross-checks this against the authenticated transport identity.

lastUserVerificationAt.description: Most recent local user-verification on the consumer device (WebAuthn UV, biometric unlock). The maintainer's policy may require this to be within N seconds.

StepUpChallenge.title: StepUpChallenge
StepUpChallenge.description: The demand half of a step-up exchange: what the maintainer returns in the `details` of a `stepUpRequired` error, naming the method the consumer must satisfy and the challenge its proof must answer. The consumer's reply is a `StepUpProof`, whose `challengeId` echoes the `challengeId` here — the two definitions are the two ends of one exchange and their `method`/`kind` vocabularies MUST stay in step. Referenced by the `detailsSchema` of `vault/release`, `vault/proxy-login`, and `vault/sign-trust-task`, which previously each restated it.

method.description: The step-up method the consumer must satisfy. Mirrors `StepUpProof.kind`.

challengeId.description: Maintainer-issued challenge id. The consumer echoes this in `StepUpProof.challengeId` so the maintainer can bind the proof to the demand that provoked it.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the challenge remains answerable. Advisory to the consumer; the maintainer enforces its own expiry.

proof.description: Format depends on kind: WebAuthn assertion (base64url), DIDComm approval-response message id, or 6–8-digit TOTP code.

challengeId.description: Maintainer-issued challenge id the proof responds to.
